name: Eliphaz
bio: Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's three friends, traveled with Bildad and Zophar to mourn with him and comfort him after disaster struck his family and health, sitting with him in silence for seven days before anyone spoke (Job 2:11-13). His lengthy speeches arguing that Job's suffering must be deserved punishment for sin are told in detail in the chapters ahead. Across three speeches (Job 4-5, 15, 22), Eliphaz argued that no one is truly innocent before God and that Job's suffering must stem from sin, growing progressively harsher — from gently urging Job to accept correction, to accusing him of undermining piety, to finally charging him outright with specific sins like oppressing the poor and withholding food from the hungry. Afterward, the LORD rebuked him for not speaking rightly about God as Job had, and had him offer sacrifices alongside Bildad and Zophar while Job prayed for them; the LORD accepted Job's prayer on their behalf (Job 42:7-9).
